Piecewise Exponential Multi-Arm Survival Time

Source: R/f_piecewise_survival_time_multiarm.R
getPiecewiseSurvivalTimeMultiArm.Rd

Creates a validated piecewise exponential survival specification for a patient-wise multi-arm simulation.

Usage

getPiecewiseSurvivalTimeMultiArm(
  piecewiseSurvivalTime = NULL,
  lambdaControl = NULL,
  hazardRatios = NULL,
  medianControl = NULL,
  medianTreatments = NULL
)

Arguments

piecewiseSurvivalTime

Numeric interval start times beginning with 0.

lambdaControl

Positive control hazards, one per interval. Specify either lambdaControl or medianControl.

hazardRatios

One active-arm-by-interval matrix, a named list of such matrices (one per situation), or an active-arm-by-interval-by-situation array. In the array, situation is the slowest-changing dimension. Specify either hazardRatios or medianTreatments.

medianControl

Positive, finite exponential control medians, one per interval, as an alternative to lambdaControl. Values are not recycled.

medianTreatments

Positive, finite exponential treatment medians, in the same matrix, list, or array format as hazardRatios, as an alternative to it.

Value

A PiecewiseSurvivalTimeMultiArm object.

Details

At least two finite, strictly increasing interval starts are required. The last interval is open-ended. Hazards must be finite and strictly positive. Group and situation names must be unique and non-empty. Unnamed groups are positional; named groups must agree in order. Interval columns are positional and receive labels derived from the interval starts. Only piecewise exponential event times are supported; simulation requires kappa = 1. The returned time definition inherits from ParameterSet and supports names(), print(), summary(), as.data.frame(), as.matrix(), and getObjectRCode(). Hazard ratios specify the data-generating distribution, rather than separate interval-specific analysis estimands. Median inputs parameterize each interval's exponential hazard through getLambdaByMedian(median, kappa = 1). They are not the actual medians of the complete piecewise survival distributions. The original interval medians are retained as user-defined parameters; hazards and hazard ratios calculated from them are marked as derived. No automatic recycling across intervals or groups is performed.

Examples

hazardRatios <- getPiecewiseHazardRatioArray(
    favorable = rbind(lowDose = c(0.9, 0.8), highDose = c(0.8, 0.6)),
    conservative = rbind(lowDose = c(1, 0.9), highDose = c(0.9, 0.75))
)
piecewiseTime <- getPiecewiseSurvivalTimeMultiArm(
    piecewiseSurvivalTime = c(0, 6),
    lambdaControl = c(0.08, 0.12),
    hazardRatios = hazardRatios
)
piecewiseTime
#> Piecewise exponential multi-arm survival time
#> 
#> 
#> Hazard ratios - favorable:
#>           interval
#> group      0 - <6 >=6
#>   lowDose     0.9 0.8
#>   highDose    0.8 0.6
#> 
#> Hazard ratios - conservative:
#>           interval
#> group      0 - <6  >=6
#>   lowDose     1.0 0.90
#>   highDose    0.9 0.75
#> Control hazards (common to all treatment arms):
#>         0 - <6  >=6
#> Control   0.08 0.12

getPiecewiseSurvivalTimeMultiArm(
    piecewiseSurvivalTime = c(0, 6),
    medianControl = c(12, 24),
    medianTreatments = rbind(lowDose = c(15, 30), highDose = c(18, 36))
)
#> Piecewise exponential multi-arm survival time
#> 
#> 
#> Treatment medians - Situation 1 (exponential per interval):
#>           interval
#> group      0 - <6 >=6
#>   lowDose      15  30
#>   highDose     18  36
#> 
#> Hazard ratios - Situation 1:
#>           interval
#> group         0 - <6       >=6
#>   lowDose  0.8000000 0.8000000
#>   highDose 0.6666667 0.6666667
#> Control hazards (common to all treatment arms):
#>             0 - <6        >=6
#> Control 0.05776227 0.02888113
#> 
#> Control medians (exponential per interval):
#>         0 - <6 >=6
#> Control     12  24
